body:
I'd suggest that we approach this in a slightly different order:

1. Solve #4611 with tests and possible specification changes so we're clear on when `unload` and `pagehide` fire in all circumstances.
2. Stop reusing the term "unload" to mean different things. (Could perhaps be done in parallel with 1, not sure.)
3. Recommend that developers use `pagehide` because of X/Y/Z. (If `unload` fires in a subset of cases I'm not sure it's a good idea to suggest a search & replace as sites might well rely on the differences.)

> Solve #4611 with tests and possible specification changes so we're clear on when unload and pagehide fire in all circumstances.

Sounds reasonable. I have a simple test for iframe unload/pagehide [here](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/2462996). That issue seems to talk about [other things](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/4611#issuecomment-560586808) such as relation with `document.open()` and ordering with nulling the browsing context though, which I'm not familiar about and need their own tests. Anyways, if my current WPT looks useful, I'll send a PR in the WPT repo.

> Stop reusing the term "unload" to mean different things. (Could perhaps be done in parallel with 1, not sure.)

It looks like the only "wrong" usage currently is just for the `unload` event. Should we add a note or something in the spec for this?

> Recommend that developers use pagehide because of X/Y/Z. (If unload fires in a subset of cases I'm not sure it's a good idea to suggest a search & replace as sites might well rely on the differences.)

I think we can suggest a pretty simple replacement strategy to web authors. If they are interested in all cases of `Document` replacement/navigation/removal (the first definition of "unload" that I mentioned), then they should just change their `unload` event listeners to `pagehide` event listeners. If they are interested only in the original "unload" cases (the second definition, where the `Document` will actually get destroyed) they can change their `unload` event listeners to `pagehide` event listeners, but filter out cases where the `persisted` bit is true.

Do you think that's reasonable? Where's the best place to put these recommendations?

---
Also, two things that I realized I forgot to include in my original post:
* We have `beforeunload` which uses the first definition of "unload", unlike the `unload` event.
* There's an additional case where `unload` won't be fired even when we will destroy the `Document`: e.g. when a page initially gets bfcached (we successfully navigate away from it), but due to some reason it gets dropped (due to memory pressure, etc).

The first point is the weirdest one, not sure what we can do about it though :(

Are browsers consistent on the `iframe` removal case? If so, it's probably worth adding a test. (I'd suggest trying to capture the event order at least and perhaps even see if they are all in the same task (and no timers can get inbetween).) If the nested document had its own nested document (or even more) that would allow testing the recursion a bit better.

With a recommendation to web authors I'm mainly worried that we'd be doing it without knowing about all cases.

As for naming, maybe it's best if we stop using "unload" altogether and only have it for the names of the events. (Or rename it to the page hide algorithm.) And explain with notes when they fire in relation to other things.

> Actualmente parece que hay dos significados distintos para "descargar" en la especificación:
> 
> * Cambiar el `Document`que está cargado actualmente: Utilizado por " [descargar un documento](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#unload-a-document) " y " [descargar pasos de cambio de visibilidad del documento](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#unloading-document-visibility-change-steps) " que se llaman en [navegaciones](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#navigating-across-documents:unload-a-document-2) ,   [recorrido del historial](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/history.html#the-history-interface:unload-a-document-2) , [cierre del contexto de navegación](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/window-object.html#close-a-browsing-context) y el `beforeunload`evento.
> * Destruir un `Document`: utilizado por el `unload`evento, que solo se activa si el `Document`ya no es recuperable (por [Hacer que beforeunload no afecte a 'salvageable' y activar el evento de descarga solo si el documento ya no es recuperable  #5889](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/5889) ).
> 
> La primera definición significa que `Document`no es necesario destruirlo si se descarga, lo que permite casos en los que la caché de avance/retroceso mantiene el `Document`objeto activo después de la navegación para que `Document`pueda reutilizarse en la navegación hacia atrás, etc.
> 
> Sin embargo, el `unload`evento no se activa cada vez que "descargamos" (usando la primera definición), sino que solo se activa cuando `Document`resulta que ya no se [puede recuperar](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#concept-document-salvageable) , lo que significa que se destruirá más tarde. Incluso usando la segunda definición, no siempre se activa: ejemplos notables incluyen cuando descartamos [un contexto de navegación](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/iframe-embed-object.html#the-iframe-element:unload-a-document) (aunque según [#4611](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/4611) esto no es cierto en la práctica, por lo que podría ser un problema aparte), y cuando `Document`se destruye mientras no es el "documento activo" (por ejemplo, cuando se guarda en bfcache pero luego se destruye debido a presión de memoria/tiempo de espera/otras razones).
> 
> Así que supongo que el problema principal aquí es que **el `unload`evento tiene un nombre engañoso** , ya que no siempre se activará cuando estemos "descargando" como se define en la primera definición (es decir, cuando se use el término "descargar" en la especificación). Además, ya tenemos el `pagehide`evento, que [siempre se activará](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#unloading-documents:event-pagehide-4) cuando estemos descargando y cubre todos los casos en los que `unload`se activa el evento (+ ¡más!). Esto significa que todos `unload`los manejadores deberían poder cambiarse a un `pagehide`manejador.
> 
> Teniendo en cuenta lo anterior, me pregunto si sería conveniente descontinuar el `unload`evento (esto no significa que los navegadores dejarán de activarlo inmediatamente; [aproximadamente el 66 %](https://www.chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/202) de las cargas de página aún utilizan `unload`controladores). Esto eliminaría cualquier confusión en torno al término "descargar".
> 
> Si eso parece demasiado drástico, supongo que podemos simplemente aclarar los diferentes significados (y tal vez MDN, etc., puedan ayudar a aclarar los casos en los que se activará el evento de descarga y en los que no).
> 
> Temas relevantes: [#5748](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/5748) , [#4611](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/4611)
